entries.ex: Rapid *urbanisation* has put enormous pressure on water and electricity supplies in developing countries.
entries.exAr: أدى *التحضر* السريع إلى ضغط هائل على إمدادات المياه والكهرباء في البلدان النامية.

entries.ex: Air quality in *urban* areas is often worse than in the countryside.
entries.exAr: غالبا ما تكون جودة الهواء في المناطق *الحضرية* أسوأ منها في الريف.

entries.ex: Young people continue to leave *rural* villages in search of better-paid work.
entries.exAr: يواصل الشباب مغادرة القرى *الريفية* بحثا عن عمل بأجر أفضل.

entries.ex: Many families move to a quiet *suburb* once they have children.
entries.exAr: تنتقل عائلات كثيرة إلى *ضاحية* هادئة بعد أن يصبح لديها أطفال.

entries.ex: The government plans to invest heavily in roads, bridges and other *infrastructure*.
entries.exAr: تخطط الحكومة لاستثمار مبالغ كبيرة في الطرق والجسور وغيرها من مرافق *البنية التحتية*.

entries.ex: Cheap and reliable *public transport* encourages people to leave their cars at home.
entries.exAr: تشجع *وسائل النقل العام* الرخيصة والموثوقة الناس على ترك سياراتهم في المنزل.

entries.ex: *Traffic congestion* costs city economies billions in lost working hours each year.
entries.exAr: يكلف *الازدحام المروري* اقتصادات المدن مليارات بسبب ساعات العمل الضائعة كل عام.

entries.ex: Thousands of employees *commute* into the capital every day from neighbouring towns.
entries.exAr: *يتنقل* آلاف الموظفين يوميا إلى العاصمة من المدن المجاورة.

entries.ex: The council has widened pavements to make the city centre safer for *pedestrians*.
entries.exAr: وسع المجلس البلدي الأرصفة لجعل وسط المدينة أكثر أمانا *للمشاة*.

entries.ex: Land is so expensive in Hong Kong that developers build *skyscrapers* rather than houses.
entries.exAr: الأراضي باهظة الثمن في هونغ كونغ إلى درجة أن المطورين يبنون *ناطحات السحاب* بدلا من المنازل.

entries.ex: There is a severe shortage of affordable *housing* for young people in major cities.
entries.exAr: هناك نقص حاد في *المساكن* الميسورة التكلفة للشباب في المدن الكبرى.

entries.ex: Many graduates spend almost half of their income on *rent*.
entries.exAr: ينفق كثير من الخريجين ما يقارب نصف دخلهم على *الإيجار*.

entries.ex: The *landlord* is responsible for repairing the heating in the flat.
entries.exAr: *المؤجر* مسؤول عن إصلاح التدفئة في الشقة.

entries.ex: New laws protect *tenants* from sudden and unfair rent increases.
entries.exAr: تحمي القوانين الجديدة *المستأجرين* من زيادات الإيجار المفاجئة وغير العادلة.

entries.ex: Families in *overcrowded* flats often have no quiet space for children to study.
entries.exAr: غالبا ما لا تجد العائلات التي تعيش في شقق *مكتظة* مكانا هادئا لدراسة الأطفال.

entries.ex: Around a quarter of the world's urban population lives in *slums* or informal settlements.
entries.exAr: يعيش نحو ربع سكان المدن في العالم في *أحياء عشوائية* أو تجمعات سكنية غير رسمية.

entries.ex: The new estate has good local *amenities*, including shops, a clinic and a mosque.
entries.exAr: يتمتع الحي السكني الجديد *بمرافق خدمية* محلية جيدة، منها متاجر وعيادة ومسجد.

entries.ex: The town lacks sports *facilities* such as swimming pools and football pitches.
entries.exAr: تفتقر البلدة إلى *المنشآت* الرياضية مثل أحواض السباحة وملاعب كرة القدم.

entries.ex: Heavy lorries are banned from *residential* streets at night.
entries.exAr: يُمنع مرور الشاحنات الثقيلة في الشوارع *السكنية* ليلا.

entries.ex: The high *cost of living* in London forces many workers to live far from their offices.
entries.exAr: تجبر *تكلفة المعيشة* المرتفعة في لندن كثيرا من العاملين على السكن بعيدا عن مكاتبهم.

entries.ex: *Urban sprawl* is swallowing farmland on the edges of many growing cities.
entries.exAr: يلتهم *الزحف العمراني* الأراضي الزراعية على أطراف كثير من المدن المتنامية.

entries.ex: Research suggests that access to *green space* improves residents' mental health.
entries.exAr: تشير الأبحاث إلى أن الوصول إلى *المساحات الخضراء* يحسن الصحة النفسية للسكان.

entries.ex: Greater Cairo is one of the largest *metropolitan* areas in Africa.
entries.exAr: تعد القاهرة الكبرى من أكبر *التجمعات الحضرية* في أفريقيا.

entries.ex: Good *town planning* places schools and clinics within walking distance of homes.
entries.exAr: يضع *التخطيط العمراني* الجيد المدارس والعيادات على مسافة يمكن قطعها سيرا من المنازل.

entries.ar: تحول الحي إلى حي راق، الاستطباق
entries.ex: *Gentrification* has forced many long-term residents out of the old harbour district.
entries.exAr: أجبر *تحول حي الميناء القديم إلى حي راق* كثيرا من سكانه القدامى على مغادرته.

entries.ex: Children are more active when their *neighbourhood* has safe places to play outdoors.
entries.exAr: يكون الأطفال أكثر نشاطا عندما يضم *حيهم* أماكن آمنة للعب في الهواء الطلق.

entries.ex: The city has more than ten million *inhabitants*, making it the largest in the country.
entries.exAr: يزيد عدد *سكان* المدينة على عشرة ملايين نسمة، مما يجعلها أكبر مدن البلاد.

entries.ex: Trains are so crowded during *rush hour* that many passengers have to stand.
entries.exAr: تكون القطارات مزدحمة جدا في *ساعة الذروة* إلى درجة أن كثيرا من الركاب يضطرون إلى الوقوف.

entries.ex: Since the city built protected *cycle lanes*, the number of cyclists has doubled.
entries.exAr: منذ أن أنشأت المدينة *مسارات دراجات* محمية، تضاعف عدد راكبي الدراجات.

entries.ex: The scheme offers grants to *homeowners* who install solar panels on their roofs.
entries.exAr: يقدم البرنامج منحا *لمالكي المنازل* الذين يركبون ألواحا شمسية على أسطح منازلهم.

gap.s: My father has to ____ for nearly two hours each day to reach his office.
The city's ____ is struggling to cope with the rapid growth in population.
Most of the town's ____ work in fishing or tourism.
As a ____, you have the right to a written contract with your landlord.
The estate lacks basic ____ such as a supermarket and a pharmacy.
The hospital is so ____ that some patients have to wait in the corridors.
The main shopping street has been closed to cars and is now for ____ only.
Living in a ____ means a quieter life but a longer journey into the city.

para.a: More and more people are moving from villages to cities.
para.b: Rapid *urbanisation* is drawing millions of people from the countryside into cities.

para.a: Cities keep growing outwards into the countryside.
para.b: *Urban sprawl* is steadily eating into the surrounding countryside.

para.a: Everything is very expensive in this city.
para.b: The *cost of living* in this city is exceptionally high.

para.a: Rich newcomers are pushing poorer families out of the area.
para.b: *Gentrification* is displacing low-income families from the area.

p1.q: Do you live in a house or a flat?
p1.a: I live in a flat on the fifth floor of a fairly new building. It's not huge, but it's comfortable, and the *neighbourhood* is quiet. There's also a park nearby, which is great for evening walks.

p1.q: How do you usually travel to work or school?
p1.a: I usually take the metro. My *commute* is about forty minutes, which isn't too bad. I avoid driving because the roads are terrible during *rush hour*, and finding a parking space is almost impossible.

p1.q: Would you prefer to live in the city or the countryside?
p1.a: At this stage of my life, definitely the city. There are more job opportunities and better *facilities*, like hospitals and universities. Maybe when I retire, I'll move somewhere *rural*, where life is slower and the air is cleaner.

p2.cue: Describe a part of your city or town that has changed a lot.
points: and explain how you feel about these changes
p2.a: I'm going to talk about the area around the old market in the centre of my home town. When I was a child, it was a run-down *neighbourhood* with narrow, dusty streets and very few *amenities*. Most of the buildings were old and quite *overcrowded*, and there was hardly any *green space* where children could play. Over the past ten years, however, it has been completely transformed. The local council invested in new *infrastructure*: the roads were repaved, and the main street was turned into a *pedestrian* zone with trees, benches and small cafés. Several old houses were restored and turned into shops and galleries. Overall, I feel quite positive about these changes, because the area is now cleaner, safer and much more attractive. That said, I have mixed feelings, too. Rents have risen sharply, and some families who had lived there for generations could no longer afford to stay. So I think development is good, but it shouldn't push out the original *inhabitants*.

p3.q: What are the main problems that people living in big cities face today?
p3.a: I'd say the biggest problem is the *cost of living*, especially housing. In many capitals, young people simply can't afford to buy a home. Then there's *traffic congestion*, which wastes hours every week and pollutes the air. And some people also feel quite isolated, because city life is so busy that they hardly know their neighbours.

p3.q: How can governments make cities better places to live in?
p3.a: I think the key is long-term *town planning*. Governments should invest in reliable *public transport* so that people don't depend on cars, and they should protect parks rather than selling the land to developers. Building affordable homes near workplaces would also help, because it shortens journeys to work and gives people more time with their families.

writing.q: In many cities around the world, rapid population growth has led to a shortage of affordable housing. What problems does this cause, and what measures could be taken to solve them? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
essay: As more people move to cities in search of work and education, rapid *urbanisation* has pushed property prices far beyond the reach of ordinary families. This essay will examine the main problems caused by the shortage of affordable *housing* and suggest some practical measures to address them.

The most serious consequence is financial pressure on households. When *rent* consumes half of a family's income, little is left for food, education or savings, and many young adults are forced to delay marriage or continue living with their parents. A second problem is poor living conditions. Low-income families often end up in *overcrowded* flats or, in developing countries, in informal *slums* that lack clean water and sanitation. Furthermore, workers who cannot afford to live near their jobs face long and exhausting journeys, which add to *traffic congestion* and air pollution.

Several measures could ease the situation. Firstly, governments could build more social housing and require private developers to include a proportion of low-cost homes in every new project. Singapore offers a successful example, as the majority of its citizens live in high-quality public flats. Secondly, laws could protect *tenants* from excessive rent increases and unfair evictions. Finally, better *town planning* and investment in *public transport* would allow people to live in cheaper areas without spending hours travelling.

In conclusion, the lack of affordable homes in growing cities causes financial hardship, poor living conditions and longer journeys to work. However, with a combination of public housing, stronger protection for renters and smarter urban planning, these problems can be significantly reduced.
